questions.question: Car drivers should know that large trucks:

options.text: Have large blind spots.
Can stop faster than passenger vehicles.
Do not need more room to turn than passenger vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have large blind spots.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have big blind spots in front, on the sides, and in back. Do not stay in these areas. Because trucks are larger and heavier, they need more space to turn and stop than regular cars.

questions.question: What is the main thinking of defensive drivers?

options.text: They trust other drivers will do the right thing.
They think about what other drivers might do and get ready to react.
They expect no help and give none.

questions.correctAnswerText: They think about what other drivers might do and get ready to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means expecting mistakes from other drivers and being prepared to handle them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Road construction ahead.
The road curves left, then right.
The road curves right, then left.
Steep hill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road ahead will curve to the right and then to the left. Slow down so you can safely navigate these curves.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway:

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
Pass only on the right.
Watch for oncoming traffic.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear and use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to go around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red lights and gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at railroad crossings when told to do so by a flagger, stop sign, gates, or flashing lights. Not all crossings have these devices. It is against the law to drive around lowered railroad gates.

questions.question: You must signal every time you pull away from a curb.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: You must use a turn signal every time you pull away from a curb.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Slow down.
Drive faster.
Drive the speed limit carefully.
Never drive faster than 20 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when rain, snow, or ice makes the road slippery. When road conditions are bad, safety may require driving slower than the posted speed limit.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines down the middle of the road mean:

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
No one can pass from either direction.
Anyone can pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one can pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean passing is not allowed from either direction. You may only cross them to make a left turn or pass pedestrians, bicyclists, scooter riders, or skateboarders when it is safe.

questions.question: Driving at night is more dangerous than driving during the day because:

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead.
The road is always more slippery at night.
Your reaction time is slower at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead.
questions.explanation: Lower visibility and glare from oncoming headlights mean you cannot see as far ahead at night as during the day. Always use headlights and be careful when driving in the dark.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Hospital.
Intersection ahead.
Railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to situations ahead. This sign warns of an upcoming intersection so you can prepare for traffic or turns.

questions.question: Interstate driving requires drivers to:

options.text: Be able to safely drive at higher speeds.
Stay alert at all times.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe interstate driving requires you to stay alert and drive safely at high speeds.

questions.question: What can you do to avoid making emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from the car in front of you.
Drive only in the right lane.
Drive slower than other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance lets you react to problems ahead without emergency stops. Emergency stops can cause the driver behind you to crash into your vehicle.

questions.question: You may park or stop on the freeway shoulder:

options.text: If you turn on your four-way emergency flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to check a map for directions.
Only in an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only in an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except during an emergency.

questions.question: You hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to come back.
Leave a note with your name and address on the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked vehicle, you must leave a note with your name, phone number, and address securely attached to the vehicle.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal whenever you move left or right. Signal when changing lanes, pulling into traffic from a parking space, or passing another vehicle.

questions.question: Strong wind on highways:

options.text: Usually only affects large vehicles.
Only causes visibility problems.
Can cause problems for all vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause problems for all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong wind affects all drivers, not just large vehicles. Wind can reduce visibility by blowing dust and dirt, and it can also physically push a vehicle off course.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, drivers must yield the right-of-way to all drivers who arrived before them.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, yield to drivers who arrived before you. Wait your turn before entering the intersection.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, it is safe to move back into the right lane:

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you cannot see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When passing, return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always check your blind spots before moving back.

questions.question: You must show proof of insurance to law enforcement:

options.text: Only if you are in a collision.
If you are in a collision or stopped for a traffic citation.
Only if you are stopped and cited.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in a collision or stopped for a traffic citation.
questions.explanation: Always keep proof of insurance with you when driving. Show your proof of insurance and license to an officer upon request during a traffic stop or after a collision.

questions.question: At an intersection with stop signs on all corners, yield the right-of-way to any driver:

options.text: On your left.
Who arrived before you.
Across from you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Who arrived before you.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles proceed in the order they arrived. If multiple vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
